title: fix(sessions): shorten write locks when deleting sessions with retained history
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes long SQLite writer holds when deleting a session that owns retained transcript windows in a large session database.

## User Impact

Session deletion releases the SQLite write lock sooner. Retained transcripts, successor ordering, and deletion refusal rules stay unchanged. No schema, configuration, migration, or index changes. The reference scan still costs CPU and occupies the worker before the transaction; this does not claim lower total request latency.

## Why This Change Was Made

The slow CTE reads surviving references to protect retained history; its rows are not deletion candidates. For requests with no transcript-removal plans, the deletion worker prepares successors before BEGIN, then the row-deletion owner uses them only while the existing database identity/revision matches. Intervening writes use the existing current-row query. Other reclamation paths and PostgreSQL keep their current behavior.

This moves planning out of the write transaction while preserving the reference parser and SQL. Request-local maps and existing callback plumbing add 52 production lines; no new cache or manager. Simplification and independent Codex review found no further safe reduction or actionable finding.

## Evidence

The two native-owner regressions fail on the baseline worker and pass with this change: the unchanged survivor scan runs before BEGIN, and a canonical intervening write forces current-row validation. Deletion/receipt/reference tests passed 54/55. The unrelated UTF-16le exclusion assertion fails identically on exact parent 932b13220bfdac6e4b191c831421e0e8772b9c3d; its encoding-dependent expectation originated in #138470 (93450a667d2a), later moved unchanged by #179786. First failing runtime version is not established.

Affected sessions browser tests passed 3/3; deletion and bulk-delete-scope browser E2E passed 6/6. Relevant runtime worker bundles built during the focused tests. Local check:changed passed every gate except its unrelated production unused-export failure, which also reproduces on the exact parent: #199338 (032227a96023) moved the last external use of INTERNAL_PLUGIN_PATH_PARAM into its defining module but retained the export. No baseline exemption was added.

Final synthetic measurement: 10,001 sessions, 1,417 optional-reference rows, parent chains of depth 256, 512 KiB metadata per reference-bearing row, five counterbalanced pairs, separate allocation and A/A controls. Paired reversible native-owner samples reduced median writer hold 1080.22→1.21 ms and p95 1106.21→1.34 ms (25 samples/arm). CPU/op 1078.47→1092.43 ms (+1.3%); sampled JS allocation/op 5,581,491→5,614,485 bytes (+0.6%). A/A baseline medians were 1101.36/1096.45 ms; allocation controls 5,620,253/5,638,205 bytes/op.

The committed candidate held the writer 6.20 ms; the exact CTE (697775172d959c1a) took 1089.46 ms and returned 1,417 survivor rows before BEGIN. Physical target deletion, unchanged survivor digest and retained-window rehoming were verified. The second plan read zero target rows and ran no survivor CTE. Before/after EXPLAIN and SQL are identical: session_nodes scan, materialized projections and JSON traversal, indexed fallback lookup, temporary ordering. No recursive tree walk. V8 sampling excludes native SQLite allocations; timing and allocation were measured separately.

Capacity gap: the local fixture is approximately 715 MiB, not a 35 GiB database; no btrfs or workspace-file claim. Exact-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43703040395. The run completed successfully on fcf985da7eb31131e3537d995868cf24a2b8473f (51 successful jobs, no failures). Final-head ClawSweeper review has zero findings/open items: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199563#issuecomment-6893035466. Merged as 649df9afd90875837fe78ade005180d6d7242d28.
